MISLEADING NARRATIVES ABOUT ELON MUSK

Here are several claims that have been widely repeated despite contradicting available facts and records:

•  “Elon grew up wealthy from an apartheid emerald mine”
 His father had a small, informal stake in a Zambian emerald operation (not a formal mine in South Africa). Elon left South Africa at 17 with limited funds and has stated he received no significant inheritance or mine profits to build his companies.

•  “Elon performed a Nazi salute” At a January 2025 event, he made a gesture (hand to chest then extended outward) while thanking the crowd. The ADL initially described it as “an awkward gesture in a moment of enthusiasm, not a Nazi salute.”

•  “Tesla vehicles catch fire more often than gas cars” Multiple data sources, including NFPA and insurance analyses, show Tesla and other EVs have significantly lower fire rates per mile driven or per vehicle sold compared to gasoline-powered vehicles (often by a factor of 10x or more).

•  “Elon didn’t found Tesla — he took it over” He joined early as a major investor and became CEO, leading the company through near-bankruptcy and scaling it globally. The original founders have publicly credited his role in building Tesla into what it is today.

•  “Elon’s companies rely on government handouts and he is a ‘welfare queen’” Tesla received government loans that were repaid early with interest. 

SpaceX has won NASA and other contracts through competitive bidding. Most major automotive and aerospace companies have received various forms of government support.

These narratives have persisted in media coverage and online discourse for years, often without full context or accurate sourcing
